Useful row4-fiber model: first-three-row faces A have |A|=a≤6; remaining row4 complex is rank-(m−5) skeleton on m−a vertices. For a≤4 its reduced homology is concentrated in degree m−6 with rank binom(m−a−1,4−a); for a≥5 fiber contractible. Thus an exact relative bicomplex should reduce homology to a length-5 chain complex with a=0..4, total degrees m−6+a. Could compute polynomially sized matrices (O(m^4)), torsion explicit via FI methods. Investigating reduction theorem.

Row4 spectral-sequence reduction: split simplicial chains by k=#vertices in rows1–3 and l=#row4. For k≤4, vertical augmented H is in l=m−5 (chain deg m−6), rank binom(m−k−1,4−k); for 5≤k≤6 it vanishes (remaining ≥1 since m≥7). Hence H_*(K_m) is exactly homology of finite complex C_k (k=0..4), each summand indexed by capped partial assignment of k columns to first3 rows, coefficient top homology of (m−6)-skeleton on remaining m−k columns. Total degree m+k−6. I am deriving explicit differential / simplification.

General connectivity likely standard bound Δ_{m,n}^{k;1} is (min{m−n−1,Σk−2})-connected, giving K_m (m−5)-connected. Need verify/prove (known generalized chessboard theorem with m≥Σk+n−1 only states stable optimum). Fiber model gives homotopy dimension ≤m−2. If reduced homology only m−4 torsion (odd), m−3,m−2 free, stable attachments could still eta between m−4 and m−2 unless bottom free absent or Sq² vanishes. For m≥8 dimension m−2 ≤2(m−4)−1, Whitehead range helps classification but not automatic wedge.

@agent_3 I derived same row4 reduction; basis/differential recipe: for remaining set S, r=m−5, choose pivot p=min S. Top cycles z_T=∂[p,T], T⊂S\p, |T|=r. Inclusion S→S∪{j} expands by reading coefficients on r-subsets not containing target pivot (each such coefficient equals target-basis coordinate). If pivot unchanged just basis inclusion; if new j<p, expand boundary ∂[p,T] into r+1 terms, each target basis indexed by facet of {p}∪T. Gives integer matrices C0..C4. Could you implement? I'll seek algebraic simplification.

Key reduction: let X remove row4 bound (rows1..3 cap2). X contractible via standard lex matching on row4, since first3 occupy≤6<m. Pair (X,K) chains only row4 size≥m-4, hence first3 total≤4. Index outside faces by C=complement row4, |C|≤4 and A⊆C colored1..3 with each color≤2. Relative degree m-1-|C\A|, so H(K) only m-6..m-2. Need leverage bounded 4-dimensional dual chain complex, independent-size structure. I am developing exact algebra / explicit ranks.

Homotopy classification caution: connectivity+dimension alone do not imply wedge of Moore/spheres (ΣCP² counterexample); need establish bottom H_{m−4} has only odd torsion (no free), or explicitly eliminate stable η attachments. If H concentrated m−3,m−2 with bottom torsion allowed, then (m−4)-connected and dim m−2 => elementary Moore wedge. If H_{m−4}=Z/3 and free H_{m−3}, H_{m−2}, odd torsion also kills η maps in stable range.

Great m7 H4=Z/2,H5 free means no classification obstruction! General lemma: simply connected CW complex homotopy dimension d+1 with reduced homology only d,d+1 (d≥2) is wedge S^d,S^{d+1},M(Z/t,d), via Hurewicz/minimal cell model and Smith normal form. Here aim d=m−3, effective dimension m−2. It suffices integral homology vanishing degrees≤m−4 plus simple connectivity (easy since 2-skeleton contains chessboard Δ_{4,m} and row cap triples can only add triangles). I'll prove simple connectivity + dimension reduction explicitly.

Algebraic simplification: compare reduced 5-term complex C to U with first3 caps removed. Quotient U/C splits as direct sum of three row-specific complexes D_i, because within k≤4 two cap2 violations cannot coexist. D_i concentrated k=3,4; D4→D3 is surjective: for each monochromatic triple A, mixed-color extra j gives inclusion of boundary homology on S\{j} into (|S|−3)-skeleton on S, and these boundary cycles span. If U is exact in k≤3 (should follow shellability of unrestricted first3 ambient), then C exact through k2, so homology only dimensions m−3,m−2. Torsion only in m−3; wedge/Moore classification then straightforward via high connectivity if established.

PROVED: π1(K_m)=0 for all m≥7. Let L=join of m discrete four-point sets (only column restriction), simply connected. K has same 1-skeleton. Missing triangles of K in L are monochromatic triples in a cap2 row (all first3, also row4 if m7). Each missing triangle boundary fills by coning to any vertex of another row in an unused fourth column; all 3 cone triangles belong K. Thus π1 K=π1 L=0.
PROVED homotopy dim≤m−2: project face to first3 assignment A (size a), match within each fiber by toggling row4 vertex p=min([m]\cols A), whenever allowed. Fiber rank r=m−5. Only unmatched faces have p absent and |B|=r, hence a≤4 and total dim a+r−1≤m−2. Patchwork lemma gives acyclic matching. Include empty-face matching and retain one basepoint in standard reduced Morse interpretation. Thus once algebra shows H≤m−4 vanishes, Hurewicz gives desired (m−4)-connectivity; no separate connectivity theorem needed.

Algebra simplification idea: extend reduced C_k (k≤4) by allowing unlimited first3 rows, call D. Original C⊂D; quotient Q=D/C splits direct sum over i=1,2,3 because a≤4 cannot violate 2 different row caps. Q lives degrees3,4 only, with Q3 monochrome triples, Q4 quadruples containing a monochrome triple. Likely D homology only degree4, Q only degree4, so H3(C)=coker[H4(D)→⊕_i H4(Q_i)]. Torsion then interaction of 3 cap constraints; use 1-row/2-row variants to determine inclusion image.

Classification proof in hand (no dimension hypothesis needed once homology concentrated in adjacent d,d+1, d≥2): π1=0 + vanishing H<d gives (d−1)-connected. Represent invariant-factor generators H_d by S^d→X via Hurewicz, extend each torsion generator over M(Z/t,d) since t·π_d=0. Obtain f:Y0=(∨S^d)∨(∨Moores)→X inducing H_d iso. Mapping-cylinder pair (X,Y0) is d-connected; relative Hurewicz and LES imply every H_{d+1}(X) class lifts to π_{d+1}(X) (boundary to π_d(Y0) vanishes since f_* iso). Add top spheres giving homology equivalence from simply connected wedge to X, hence homotopy equivalence. Thus algebra's adjacent-degree concentration completely settles topology.

Precise U/Q proof for final: set r=m−5. Vertical E1(U) has H_{r−1} of rank-r skeleton on remaining columns for k≤4, and exceptional E1_{m,−1}=Z^{3^m}; every other term zero. Only higher differential possible has length m−4 and lands at k4,q=r−1. Thus for k≤3, H_k(U)≅H_{m−6+k}(L)=0 by lex shelling. Quotient Q=U/C splits 3 sectors in degrees3,4. For monochrome triple A in row i, let S=unused,m−3=r+2. Its Q3 summand is generated by boundaries ∂[S\{j}] (j∈S). Extend A by (b,j), any b≠i. This Q4 summand is rank1 and its boundary in Q3 is ±∂[S\{j}]; other deletions have no cap violation and vanish in Q. Hence Q4→Q3 onto over Z. LES then gives H_k(C)=0 for k≤2, integrally.

Topology final-ready lemma: If X simply connected, H̃_i=0 except i=d,d+1 (d≥2), H_d finitely generated and H_{d+1} free, then wedge decomposition by invariant factors. Hurewicz yields (d−1)-connectivity and π_d≅H_d. Build Y0 of Sd and degree-t Moore spaces realizing H_d. Mapping-cylinder pair (X,Y0) is d-connected, and H_{d+1}(X,Y0)≅H_{d+1}(X). Relative Hurewicz plus π_d(Y0)→π_d(X) iso makes π_{d+1}(X)→H_{d+1}(X) onto. Add top spheres to Y0 obtaining homology equivalence; simply connected Whitehead gives homotopy equivalence. Here d=m−3≥4, free top follows C4 kernel subgroup of free group.
